**R2 completeness findings** (CG-R2-MIN-01, CG-R2-MIN-02, CG-R2-nit-01) were not targeted by fix-round-2 — carried forward unchanged.

findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) still reads 'Commit status context = scp/policy-check' unconditionally. The implementation correctly documents that the actual GitHub check context is '{calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check' (workflow lines 43-44), but the governing plan text remains technically inaccurate. An implementor reading only the plan spec for 020D2 branch-protection configuration will receive wrong information. Fix-round-2 did not amend the plan file.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/policy-check.yml lines 43-44: '# GitHub records reusable-workflow checks as "{calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check". / # 020D1/020D2 must verify the combined context before configuring branch protection.' The workflow correctly qualifies the context; WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) as documented in the plan does not. Fix-round-2 changes were confined to append_github_env_multiline, control-character validation, and bypass_record population — no plan-file amendment landed. Gap persists from fix-round-1/review-completeness.json finding CG-R2-MIN-01.
findings.impact: An implementor reading WP-SCP-020 §4 criterion (xi) as the authoritative spec for 020D2 configuration may hardcode 'scp/policy-check' as the required-status-check context without performing the 020E.a empirical verification. If the 020D1 caller job name is not aligned with the convention the required check will be permanently unsatisfied and the entire enforcement model will silently fail.
findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) to state the full GitHub check context format ({calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check) and require 020D2 to use the empirically verified combined string from 020E.a canary evidence before configuring branch protection. Amendment is outside 020B scope_boundary; tracked-forward into 020D2 dispatch-package instruction. No code change required for 020B.

findings.claim: The bypass gate selects only the FIRST deny finding's rule_id (workflow lines 244-250 exit via SystemExit(0) after the first match). If multiple deny findings are present and scp_bypass=true, subsequent deny findings remain in effective_denies and the workflow fails even after a valid bypass pairing passes. This single-bypass-per-invocation behaviour is not documented in the workflow, dispatch-package notes, or any tracked-forward item for ADOPT-001 §12. Fix-round-2 did not alter the selection logic or add documentation.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 244-250: for loop over payload calls print(finding['rule_id']) then raise SystemExit(0) on the first deny with a non-empty rule_id. Lines 369-371: effective_denies = [item for item in denies if not (bypass_approved and bypass_rule_id and item.get('rule_id') == bypass_rule_id)] — filters only the single SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID. append_github_env_multiline and bypass_record changes in fix-round-2 did not touch either code block. Gap persists from fix-round-1/review-completeness.json finding CG-R2-MIN-02.
findings.impact: An adopter with two concurrent deny findings (e.g., SCP-R-001 and SCP-R-003) who activates scp_bypass=true and provides a waivers.json entry for SCP-R-001 will observe: bypass gate passes for SCP-R-001; the workflow still fails because SCP-R-003 remains in effective_denies. The SCP-E004 annotation reports bypass active 'until {expires_at}' while the check fails — this will be diagnosed as a workflow bug without documented single-bypass semantics in ADOPT-001 §12.
findings.mitigation: Add a workflow comment after line 250: '# Bypass covers only the first deny finding; PRs with multiple concurrent deny findings require each rule to be addressed independently or sequentially.' Add a tracked-forward note in the 020H part 3 dispatch-package requiring ADOPT-001 §12 to document the single-bypass-per-invocation model. Comment can land in a subsequent fix-round; the 020H documentation dependency is the load-bearing tracked-forward item.

If the grep and sed are correct for the actual table format (4-digit D-0NNN), the schema pattern rejects every extracted decision_id and validate-summary fails on every break-glass run.
findings.evidence: schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json line 169: "pattern": "^D-[0-9]{3}$" (matches D-001 to D-999, exactly 3 digits). verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 33: grep -E '^\+\|\s*D-0[0-9]{3}\s*\|' (matches D-0000 to D-0999 table rows). verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 105: sed -E 's/^\+\|\s*(D-0[0-9]{3}).*/\1/' (captures D-0NNN group, 4 digits). If DECISIONS.md rows contain D-021 (3-digit), the grep at line 33 cannot match them (D-021 does not satisfy D-0[0-9]{3}). If rows contain D-0021 (4-digit), grep and sed extract D-0021, but ^D-[0-9]{3}$ rejects D-0021 (4 digits). The R2 correctness lens closed MAJ-BYPASS-003 accepting the grep pattern; the schema bypass_record.decision_id pattern was introduced in fix-round-2 separately without explicit cross-reference to the grep pattern.
findings.impact: If the format assumption is wrong, every break-glass attempt either fails at the pairing script (grep finds no matching D-NNN row) or at schema validation (decision_id fails pattern check), silently disabling the break-glass mechanism. R2 correctness and safety lenses reviewed verify-bypass-pairing.sh in detail without flagging this as a blocker, suggesting the actual estate format is consistent with the grep pattern. The completeness gap is the absence of any documentary statement of the authoritative format width.
findings.mitigation: Add a comment to verify-bypass-pairing.sh at line 33 and a '$comment' annotation or description to schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json stating the expected DECISIONS.md D-NNN column format (e.g., 'DECISIONS.md table rows use D-0NNN four-digit zero-padded format matching D-0[0-9]{3}; schema pattern D-[0-9]{3} matches the three-digit portion D-NNN'). Alternatively, align grep, sed capture, and schema pattern to use the same digit count. Non-blocking given R2 correctness lens acceptance. Tracked-forward: confirm authoritative DECISIONS.md format in 020D2 or 020E.a dispatch-package notes.

Two-pronged fix in fix-round-2. (1) Control-character validation: workflow lines 257-263 pass BYPASS_RULE_ID as a shell argument to python3; sys.argv[1] receives the full value including any embedded newlines; all(ch not in rule_id for ch in ("
","","\x00")) rejects the value and exits 1, triggering the emit_error SCP-E004 path before the pairing script or any GITHUB_ENV write is reached. (2) Safe heredoc write: append_github_env_multiline at lines 309-319 generates a collision-safe delimiter via uuidgen | tr -d '-' with a while-loop guard, then writes printf '%s<<%s
%s
%s
' key delim value delim >> GITHUB_ENV — the GitHub Actions heredoc multiline format which encapsulates the value between delimiter lines, preventing any embedded character from injecting additional KEY=VALUE pairs. All four SCP_BYPASS_* vars (lines 322-325) use this function. SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED is written via plain printf 'SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED=true
' (line 322) which carries no injection risk since the value is a literal constant.

Two complementary changes in fix-round-2. (1) Build step (lines 476-488): bypass_emitted is computed from SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED env var; when true, bypass_record dict is built from os.environ.get for all four required schema fields (rule_id, decision_id, waiver_expires_at, emitted_at); missing = [key for key, value in bypass_record.items() if not value] guards against empty fields and exits SCP-E001 with a named field list before writing the summary; summary['bypass_record'] = bypass_record is appended. (2) Schema constraint: policy-check-summary.schema.json lines 149-179 define bypass_record with required fields rule_id (minLength:1), decision_id (pattern ^D-[0-9]{3}$), waiver_expires_at (format:date-time), emitted_at (format:date-time) and additionalProperties:false; allOf at lines 236-253 requires bypass_record when bypass_emitted=true; validate-summary step (lines 493-528, if:always()) runs Draft202012Validator with FormatChecker and gates artifact upload on success. waivers_applied is not written by the bypass gate (it remains [] from scaffold initialisation), but the bypass_record field in the summary is the canonical machine-readable bypass audit record per the updated schema design.

self_reported_concerns: CG-R3-nit-01 is raised because the schema and sed patterns are structurally inconsistent at the character level. However, two prior lenses (R2 correctness and R2 safety) reviewed verify-bypass-pairing.sh in detail and accepted the grep/sed logic as correct for the actual estate DECISIONS.md format. The completeness lens cannot determine the authoritative format without reading DECISIONS.md directly. The nit verdict reflects this uncertainty.

The append_github_env_multiline while-loop termination is safe in practice: BYPASS_RULE_ID passes the control-character check (no newlines, so single-line), making a line-exact collision with a 44-character key_<32hex> delimiter statistically impossible; decision_id/waiver_expires_at/emitted_at are fixed-format single-line values. The termination guarantee is sound but undocumented inside the function body.

The missing-field check at build step lines 484-487 validates all four bypass_record fields are non-empty strings but does not pre-validate decision_id against ^D-[0-9]{3}$ before writing the summary. If decision_id is malformed, validate-summary will fail with an opaque jsonschema pattern-mismatch error rather than a named SCP-E001 message. This is a correctness-lens observation noted here for cross-lens completeness only.
structured_review.summary: R3 completeness/governance review of slice 020B after fix-round-2. Both targeted R2 MAJ closures are verified. MAJ-R2-BYPASS-001 (GITHUB_ENV heredoc + newline-strip on rule_id): closed by two-pronged fix — Python control-character validation at workflow lines 257-263 rejects rule_ids containing \n/\r/\x00 before the pairing script is called; append_github_env_multiline at lines 309-319 uses uuidgen-based heredoc delimiter (collision-safe while loop) for all four SCP_BYPASS_* GITHUB_ENV writes at lines 322-325, encapsulating any value safely regardless of content. MAJ-R2-BYPASS-002 (bypass_record schema field populated when bypass_emitted): closed — build step lines 476-488 conditionally constructs bypass_record dict from SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID / SCP_BYPASS_DECISION_ID / SCP_BYPASS_EXPIRES_AT / SCP_BYPASS_EMITTED_AT env vars when bypass_emitted=true; missing-field guard exits SCP-E001 on any empty field before writing; schema allOf constraint at lines 236-253 enforces bypass_record presence; validate-summary step gates artifact upload on schema validity. Three findings from the R2 completeness lens (CG-R2-MIN-01, CG-R2-MIN-02, CG-R2-nit-01) were not targeted by fix-round-2 and remain open at MIN/nit severity.
